ideas.title: Blow glass: breath, heat and gravity shape the bubble
ideas.critique: This is round 1's furnace idea with a full 3D viscous sheet in place of the axisymmetric shell. That is a real step: the player can tip and turn the pipe, a lopsided bubble refracts lopsided, and the wall bursts where it actually got too thin. The danger is the solver itself. Batty-style viscous shells on a triangle mesh are a research codebase, and if the remeshing or the burst gets faked, what remains is a glowing ball that swells on a timer and ends as one more vase-shaped prop.

ideas.title: Smash pots, and the shards fit back only where they broke
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: This answers round 1's worry about a scripted mend: shards now join only where their broken edges coincide, and the gold seams follow the real crack lines, so each jug records its own fall. Element-splitting fracture tends to give shards that follow the mesh lines and look like the mesh rather than clay, and fitting 3D shards together with a mouse may be fiddly. The slow-motion film of one falling jug is still close to the island's films of a single object.

ideas.title: A sandcastle against the tide
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: MPM sand whose cohesion depends on moisture is new physics with a strong game loop: build, race the tide, watch your choices hold or slump. Rising tides and runs of waves are things a player comes back to. The scope is the risk: MPM, saturation spreading through the sand, tide and Maelstrom waves all coupled live is several sessions of work. A cheap version, a heightfield that erodes under a timed water line, would read as the island being flooded again.

ideas.title: Ink that runs: a letter, then rain
ideas.critique: This is round 1's ink letter, now with rain and pigments that separate as they run. Colours walking different distances is a real chromatography effect, and a macro traced film of a word blooming is a fresh picture. As play it is write, then wait for weather. Paper sheets have featured on the island many times, and the friend who receives the letter is still unaddressed.

ideas.title: Candles you dip, that burn down for real
ideas.critique: Layers whose thickness depends on dip speed, and wax that melts and runs down the windward side, give the island a night light that is earned, and flames whose flicker follows the wax supply suit the path tracer. The dipping is a repeat-a-click minigame. Burning down is something to watch in time-lapse, not to play, and five chained models (Landau-Levich films, melt, film flow, flame, bending) will each be thin, so the likely result is a pretty night film with little to hold it up.
